A feature release that syncs the SDK with Python SDK v0.2.160 (from v0.2.140).
It fixes hooks, permission prompts and SDK MCP calls being lost in the turn a
background subagent wakes, and adds `verbatimPrompts` and a system-prompt
`snapshot` setting.

## ⚠️ Behavior and compatibility changes

**The 60-second cap on keeping stdin open is gone.** When hooks, a `canUseTool`
callback or SDK MCP servers are configured, `ClaudeSDK.query(...)` keeps stdin
open so the CLI can call back into your code. Java still capped that wait at
`CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT` (60s by default), a timeout the Python SDK
dropped long ago. The cap cut off any background agent that ran longer than a
minute, and its hooks were then silently skipped. The wait is now bounded only
by the between-turns ceiling described below. `CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT`
now only sets the `initialize` timeout, as it does in Python.

**Two records gained a component.** `SystemPromptPreset` gains `snapshot`, and
the internal `SDKControlInitializeRequest` gains `systemPromptSnapshot`. The
existing constructors remain, so source that calls them compiles unchanged.
Code that deconstructs these records with record patterns, or that was compiled
against the old canonical constructors, needs a recompile.

## Highlights

**A background subagent's follow-up turn is now served**
([Python #1279](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1279),
issue #1190). A `result` ends a turn, not the run. When a background subagent
finishes just before that result, its completion wakes the parent for another
turn, and that turn's `PreToolUse` hooks, permission prompts and SDK MCP calls
need stdin. The SDK used to close stdin at that first result, so the hook calls
failed and were treated as denials. Now:

- The transport sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_READS_SESSION_STATE=1`, unless you have
  already set it in any letter case.
- The SDK closes stdin when the CLI reports the session `idle`, not at the
  first result.
- The `session_state_changed` frames the SDK asked for (marked
  `sdk_host_only`) are kept out of your message stream.
- The wait between turns is bounded by `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`,
  the CLI's own background-wait ceiling: 10 minutes by default, `0` for no
  limit. It is read from `options.env` first, then the process environment.
  The clock pauses while a turn is running, while a request is being
  answered, and while a tracked agent is still in flight.
- In a streamed `ClaudeSDK.query(Iterator, ...)`, each prompt now waits for its
  own run.

> **CLI support is still rolling out.** Claude Code 2.1.283 does not yet
> honor `CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_READS_SESSION_STATE`, so with it the SDK sees no
> state frames and stdin still closes at the first result, exactly as with the
> Python SDK. To get the fix with such a CLI, opt in yourself; the frames then
> also reach your iterator:
>
> ```java
> ClaudeAgentOptions.builder()
>     .env(Map.of("CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS", "1"))
> ```
>
> Verified live against 2.1.283: with the opt-in, the follow-up turn's hook
> was served in 3 of 3 runs, and without it the run failed 1 time in 3.

**`verbatimPrompts`**
([Python #1269](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1269)).
Claude Code normally expands an `@/absolute/path` in prompt text into that
file's contents and runs a leading `/command` as a slash command. That is right
for text a user typed. It is not right for text your application assembled
from elsewhere, such as earlier turns, tool results or third-party content.
`verbatimPrompts(true)` marks every prompt the SDK sends `client_composed`, so
it is delivered exactly as written:

```java
ClaudeAgentOptions options = ClaudeAgentOptions.builder()
    .verbatimPrompts(true)
    .build();
```

It applies to `ClaudeSDK.query` string and streamed prompts, and to
`ClaudeSDKClient.connect(String)`, `query(String)` and `query(Iterator)`. While
it is on, it overrides any `client_composed` value on a message; for per-turn
control, leave it off and set the field on individual streamed messages. It
requires Claude Code 2.1.248 or later, and the SDK logs a warning on older
CLIs.

**System prompt `snapshot`**
([Python #1268](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1268)).
By default a session records its system prompt on the first request and reuses
it, even after resume. A changed prompt or `append` text therefore has no
effect until the session is compacted or a new one starts. Set `snapshot` to
`false` to rebuild the prompt on every request, which helps while you iterate
on its wording:

```java
.systemPrompt(SystemPromptCustom.of("You are a release bot.", false))
// or
.systemPrompt(SystemPromptPreset.claudeCode("Be concise.").withSnapshot(false))
```

`SystemPromptCustom` is new: a custom prompt, sent as `--system-prompt` like a
plain string, that can also carry `snapshot`. The setting requires Claude Code
2.1.257 or later.

## Also in this release

- **New examples:** `VerbatimPromptsExample` and `BackgroundAgentHooksExample`,
  the Java counterparts of the Python SDK's new e2e tests. `SystemPromptExample`
  gains a `snapshot` demo, and the README gains a "System Prompt" section.
- **`DynamicControlExample`** now switches models by the `haiku` alias, because
  the CLI rejects retired model IDs.
- **Javadoc corrections**, aligned with the Python SDK's docstring pass:
  - `SessionStore`, `MirrorErrorMessage`, `SandboxSettings`, `stopTask`,
    `rewindFiles`, `getServerInfo` and `PermissionMode.AUTO` no longer make
    outdated or wrong claims.
  - The `env`, `settings`, `mcpServers` and `sandbox` builder docs now describe
    what the transport actually does with each.
  - The custom-`Transport` overloads say which options a custom transport does
    not receive.
- **Tests:** 1118, up from 1056. They cover the run-end rules (23 cases), and a
  stand-in CLI launched as a real subprocess exercises the transport, frame
  filtering and time limit end to end.
